svg.title: BCBC 2024 · 9.23.9.8 Support of Walls
svg.text: BCBC 2024 · DIVISION B · PART 9 HOUSING AND SMALL BUILDINGS · SECTION 9.23 WOOD-FRAME CONSTRUCTION
Support of Walls

g.text: Loadbearing, parallel: on a beam or wall
Loadbearing, at right angles, no floor

svg.text: WHAT THE CODE REQUIRES
Non-loadbearing walls parallel to the floor joists are
supported by joists beneath the wall or on blocking between
the joists.
Blocking for the support of non-loadbearing walls is
(a) not less than 38 mm by 89 mm lumber, and (b) except as
required for the fastening of walls constructed with required
braced wall panels, spaced not more than 1.2 m apart.
Except as provided in Sentence (6), non-loadbearing interior
walls at right angles to the floor joists are not restricted
as to location.
Loadbearing interior walls parallel to floor joists are
supported by beams or walls of sufficient strength to safely
transfer the specified live loads to the vertical supports.
Unless the joist size is designed to support such loads,
loadbearing interior walls at right angles to floor joists
are located
(a) not more than 900 mm from the joist support where the wall
does not support a floor, and (b) not more than 600 mm from the
joist support where the wall supports one or more floors.
Loadbearing and non-loadbearing walls constructed with
required braced wall panels are continuously supported by
floor joists, blocking or rim joists to allow for the
required fastening (see Table 9.23.3.4.).
Drawn: subfloor omitted, supports in yellow. E and F: distance drawn face to face, the Article does not say how it is measured.
Source: BCBC 2024, Division B, Article 9.23.9.8. (page 9-181)
